title: Data collection, quality & lineage
summary: Build trustworthy training and evaluation datasets from raw records.
html:
Build trustworthy training and evaluation datasets from raw records.

How the pieces connect

Define the unit of data

A row might represent an event, person, document, conversation, or device. Decide the unit of prediction and the time at which features would actually be known. Keep stable identifiers so related records can be grouped and traced. A target derived from future outcomes must not leak into features.

Quality is task-specific

Validate schema, ranges, missingness, duplicates, timestamps, encoding, and class balance. Inspect representative raw examples after each transformation. A perfectly formatted dataset may omit the very cases that matter most. Maintain separate tests for structural validity and semantic correctness.

Lineage makes results explainable

Record source, collection date, consent or permitted-use metadata where relevant, transformation versions, and dataset hashes. When a source changes, lineage identifies affected examples and models. Version labels and splits as well as raw inputs. Preserve the difference between original observations and synthetic examples.

Dataset documentation

Describe intended use, collection process, known gaps, language coverage, annotator instructions, and maintenance responsibility. Document who is missing. Restrict access to sensitive records and minimize retention. A model card cannot compensate for unknown training data provenance.

Worked example

For a support-ticket classifier, split by customer or conversation when related messages share content. If a follow-up response includes the final resolution, using that response to predict the original ticket’s priority would give the model information unavailable at prediction time.

What goes wrong

Deduplicating only exact strings misses paraphrases and templates. Conversely, aggressive deduplication can remove legitimate minority patterns.

Check your understanding

Why version the train/test split?

Reveal the explanation

A changed split changes what success means. Without a fixed split identity, model comparisons can accidentally compare different tasks.

An operating model for data collection, quality & lineage

Data work is system design, not a preparatory chore. Labels reflect a process, sources change, and rows may represent related events rather than independent samples. A dataset that cannot explain where a record came from, when it was available, and how it was transformed cannot support a reliable model comparison.

The gotcha. A clean workflow diagram describes dependency order. It does not prove that any boundary is correct; each transition needs its own observable acceptance test.

Worked system: the label that arrives from the future

A support-ticket system wants to predict escalation at the moment a ticket is created. The final resolution, agent notes, and later customer messages may be excellent predictors—but none exists when the original decision is made. Including them creates a model that looks strong offline and fails at the exact moment it is meant to help. This is temporal leakage, and it survives ordinary random train/test splits because both halves can contain information from the future relative to their rows.

Build the dataset around an explicit “as-of” time. For every field, record when it became available, who produced it, and whether it can be revised. Split by time or by entity when the deployment demands it. A clean schema is not enough: the semantic lifetime of a value is part of the model.

Notebook: Make the split an explicit artifact

Treat a data contract like an API contract: validate it automatically and assign an owner. Store a small, reviewed fixture set of raw examples to catch semantic regressions that schema tests miss.

train_ids = set(train["record_id"])
assert not train_ids & set(test["record_id"])
assert train["event_time"].max() <= cutoff
# Fit transformations only after this boundary exists.
What to test next. 1. Collect: Record source, permissions, time, and unit of observation. 2. Validate: Check schema, content, gaps, duplicates, and labels. 3. Version: Freeze inputs, transformations, and split identity. 4. Maintain: Track drift, corrections, access, and retirement.

The gotcha. A small inspection script proves only the quantities it prints. Preserve units, shapes, versions, and the input fixture beside its output.

A rigorous way to practice

  1. Collect. Record source, permissions, time, and unit of observation.
  2. Validate. Check schema, content, gaps, duplicates, and labels.
  3. Version. Freeze inputs, transformations, and split identity.
  4. Maintain. Track drift, corrections, access, and retirement.

Verification questions for data collection, quality & lineage

BoundaryQuestionEvidence
CollectWhat would show that this boundary failed?Record source, permissions, time, and unit of observation.
ValidateWhat would show that this boundary failed?Check schema, content, gaps, duplicates, and labels.
VersionWhat would show that this boundary failed?Freeze inputs, transformations, and split identity.
MaintainWhat would show that this boundary failed?Track drift, corrections, access, and retirement.

The gotcha. Passing each component check separately does not prove the composed path preserves identity, units, ordering, or authority.

Lineage must answer what happened to one record

A usable lineage chain connects source identity, collection time, consent or license, schema version, transformations, labels, splits, and every derived artifact.

  • The unit of observation sets independence. Rows can describe events from the same person, device, document, or session and must often remain in one split.
  • Event time differs from processing time. Backfills and late arrivals can make a feature available in a warehouse long before it would have existed at prediction time.
  • Deletion must propagate. Removing raw data while retaining features, embeddings, caches, exports, and training subsets does not complete the lifecycle.
  • Version content, not only paths. Immutable hashes and manifests distinguish two datasets written to the same location.

The gotcha. A reproducible pipeline can reproduce an unlawfully collected, leaked, or semantically invalid dataset.
